title: Realization-independent integral factors
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put
$q=p^a$, $k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Let
$X_0/k_0$ be smooth, proper,
geometrically connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and
put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Fix an indeterminate $T$. For every prime
$\ell\neq p$, let
$(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ be the
smooth-proper
cohomological family. The reciprocal-root multiset is interpreted using the
ordinary and reciprocal-root
convention, and each $P_{i,\ell}$ is the determinant factor in that
cohomological family, explicitly

$$
P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell}).
$$

Let $Z(X_0,T)$ be the
point-count zeta series, and write
$Z(X_0,T)=A(T)/B(T)$ with $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$, $A(0)=B(0)=1$,
$\gcd(A,B)=1$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$; this is a chosen presentation satisfying
the normalized integral-fraction
conditions. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}$. For each
$\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure
$\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, set
$\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)} =\{\alpha\in\Qlb:\alpha\text{ is algebraic over }\mathbf Q\}$, the
algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q$
inside $\Qlb$, and choose an isomorphism
$\jmath_\ell:\overline{\mathbf Q}\xrightarrow{\sim} \overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}$.
For $C\in\{A,B\}$, put
$r_C=\deg C$ and define its reciprocal polynomial by

$$
C^\#(U)=U^{r_C}C(U^{-1}).
$$

For each $0\leq i\leq2d$, form the multiset $R_i$ of those roots of
$A^\#$ when $i$ is odd and of $B^\#$ when $i$ is even
that are $q$-Weil numbers of weight $i$. Put

$$
Q_i(T)=\prod_{\alpha\in R_i}(1-\alpha T)\in\mathbf Z[T].
$$

These $Q_i$ are candidate normalized integral factors.
For every
prime $\ell\neq p$, every ell-adic realization
$\jmath_\ell:\overline{\mathbf Q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}$,
and every $0\leq i\leq2d$, write
$Q_i^{(\ell,\jmath_\ell)}$ for the scalar extension of $Q_i$ along
$\jmath_\ell$.
Then scalar extension identifies the reciprocal-root multiset of $Q_i$ with
that of $P_{i,\ell}$:

$$
Q_i^{(\ell,\jmath_\ell)}(T)=P_{i,\ell}(T).
$$

Here $Q_i^{(\ell,\jmath_\ell)}$ means coefficientwise extension along
$\jmath_\ell:\overline{\mathbf Q}\xrightarrow{\sim} \overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}$, so the displayed equality is an equality in
the chosen algebraic closure of $\Ql$ (with $P_{i,\ell}$ viewed through
$\Ql\subset\Qlb$).
Consequently, after these scalar identities are established, each $Q_i$ is
the normalized
integral Frobenius factor
for the common realization.
These scalar identities are independent of the chosen realization and
preserve the normalization $Q_i(0)=1$. If
$N_\ell(T)=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\ i\ {\rm odd}}}P_{i,\ell}(T)$ and
$D_\ell(T)=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\ i\ {\rm even}}}P_{i,\ell}(T)$, the
parity-product construction gives
$A^{(\ell)}=N_\ell$ and $B^{(\ell)}=D_\ell$.
The scalar-extension notation is coefficientwise extension of integral
polynomials.

proof.text: Fix $\ell\ne p$ and put $K=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. The geometric clause (3) of [prop-trace-determinant], applied to the given smooth-proper family, gives $Z_\ell D_\ell=N_\ell$ in $\mathbf Q_\ell[[T]]$, where $Z_\ell$ is the coefficientwise image of the point-count series. It also gives the same rational identity in $\mathbf Q_\ell(T)$. Extending coefficients gives $Z_KD_\ell=N_\ell$ in $K[[T]]$. Here and below the determinant factors and parity products are viewed in $K[T]$. We use the already chosen normalized integral presentation $BZ=A$ from the hypothesis, in the exact Taylor-series sense of [def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction]; existence of a presentation is not an additional conclusion needed in this proof.

source.place: Step 1: trace-to-determinant identity; Step 3: given normalized presentation

proof.text: For every isomorphism $\iota:K\simeq\mathbf C$, [lem-weil-smooth-proper-purity-hypotheses] supplies exceptional-adjoint admissibility, the canonical functorial dualizing Weil lift, and finite-dimensional cohomology with its induced Frobenius. Thus all extra hypotheses of [thm-weil-deligne-purity] hold, and its eigenvalue clause gives absolute value $q^{i/2}$ on $H^i(X,K)$. The Frobenius-equivariant scalar-extension isomorphism and determinant equality of [lem-weil-cohomology-scalar-extension-qlbar], together with [prop-weil-reciprocal-roots-eigenvalues], therefore give $|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$ for every reciprocal root $\alpha$ of $P_{i,\ell}$. The choice of $\iota$ was arbitrary, so this conclusion holds for every such isomorphism, with the same polynomial and the same index $i$.

source.place: Step 2: purity input, with its hypotheses discharged

proof.text: Choose one such $\iota$ (the extension assertion of [lem-embedding-extension] with the number field $\mathbf Q$ supplies one). Apply [prop-weight-separation] using step 2 and the rational identity of step 1. It says that distinct $P_{i,\ell}$ are coprime in $K[T]$, that $N_\ell,D_\ell$ are coprime with constant coefficients one, and that their ordinary-root multisets are separated by the reciprocal-root absolute values $q^{i/2}$. These conclusions hold for every $\ell\ne p$.

Write $a=A_K$, $b=B_K$, $N=N_\ell$, $D=D_\ell$. By [def-weil-coprime-polynomials], coprimality of $A,B$ gives a Bezout identity over $\mathbf Q[T]$; coefficient extension preserves it by [lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-injective], so $a,b$ are coprime over $K$. The identities $bZ_K=a$ and $DZ_K=N$ give $aD=bN$ as power series and hence as polynomials by [def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series]. By [lem-weil-coprime-divides-product], first with $(x,y,z)=(a,b,N)$ and then with $(N,D,a)$, we get $a\mid N$ and $N\mid a$. Thus $N=ca$ for a unit $c$ of $K[T]$: if $N=ah$ and $a=Nk$, cancellation of the nonzero $a$ gives $hk=1$. Units of $K[T]$ are nonzero constants, as in the coprimality definition. Substitution in $aD=bN$ and cancellation give $D=cb$. Evaluating $N=ca$ at zero gives $1=c$, since $a(0)=N(0)=1$. Hence $A_K=N_\ell$ and $B_K=D_\ell$. The coefficientwise inclusion $\mathbf Q_\ell[T]\hookrightarrow K[T]$ is injective by the same extension lemma, so this also proves the required parity identities over $\mathbf Q_\ell$.

Fix any realization $\jmath:\overline{\mathbf Q}\simeq\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}$. For $C=A$ or $B$, apply [lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization] to $C\in\mathbf Q[T]$ over $\overline{\mathbf Q}$. It gives $C=\prod_\alpha(1-\alpha T)$ with the roots of $C^\#$ counted with their multiplicities; all $\alpha$ are nonzero. Map this finite product along $\jmath$ using [lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-injective]. Since $\jmath$ fixes rational coefficients, this is a factorization of $C_K$. Also factor each $P_{j,\ell}$ by the same root-factorization lemma. By step 4, multiplication of the odd factors gives $A_K$ and multiplication of the even factors gives $B_K$. Uniqueness up to reordering in that lemma now identifies, with multiplicities, the images of the roots of $C^\#$ with the multiset union of reciprocal roots of the corresponding $P_{j,\ell}$. Step 3 ensures that a root belongs to only one degree $j$.

source.place: Step 3 and Intrinsic weights: reciprocal roots of the parity products

proof.text: Every root $\alpha$ of $A^\#$ or $B^\#$ has an intrinsic weight. To see this, choose one prime $\ell\ne p$ (take $2$ unless $p=2$, then $3$) and one of the realizations fixed in the statement. Step 5 places $\jmath(\alpha)$ in exactly one $P_{j,\ell}$. The field $L=\mathbf Q(\jmath(\alpha))$ is a number field: $\jmath(\alpha)$ is algebraic over $\mathbf Q$ since it is a root of $C^\#\in\mathbf Q[U]$, and [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis] gives finiteness of this simple extension. For any $\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$, set $\sigma=\tau\circ(\jmath|_{\mathbf Q(\alpha)})^{-1}:L\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$. The first clause of [lem-embedding-extension] extends this particular $\sigma$ to $\iota:K\simeq\mathbf C$. Step 2 applies to that $\iota$ without changing the factor index $j$ and yields $|\tau(\alpha)|=|\iota(\jmath(\alpha))|=q^{j/2}$. This is the condition of [def-weil-numbers] for every $\tau$. Its weight is unique: $q=p^a>1$, so the numbers $q^{j/2}$ for $0\le j\le2d$ are strictly increasing. The index has the parity of $C$ by step 5. This proves the embedded intrinsic-weight assertion without using the theorem being proved.

source.place: Intrinsic weights of the reciprocal roots: extension of an arbitrary embedding

proof.text: The last clause of [lem-embedding-extension] says the $q$-Weil condition is Galois-stable. Step 6 supplies the unique-weight hypothesis for the chosen normalized integral fraction. Therefore [prop-galois-weight-strata] gives Galois stability, with multiplicities, of every $R_i$. In exactly this situation, [prop-galois-weight-strata-integrality] gives $Q_i=\prod_{\alpha\in R_i}(1-\alpha T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$, and [prop-galois-weight-strata-identification] says its reciprocal-root multiset is exactly $R_i$. We use these statements, including their rationality and integrality conclusions, rather than assuming integrality from an ell-adic lattice.

source.place: Step 4: Galois stability, integrality, and stratum root identification

proof.text: Return to an arbitrary $\ell\ne p$ and arbitrary $\jmath$. The multiset bijection in step 5 sends a root $\alpha$ of intrinsic weight $i$ to a reciprocal root of some $P_{j,\ell}$ of the same parity. Choose any $\iota:K\simeq\mathbf C$. Its composite with $\jmath|_{\mathbf Q(\alpha)}$ is a complex embedding of $\mathbf Q(\alpha)$, so the definition of intrinsic weight gives $|\iota(\jmath(\alpha))|=q^{i/2}$. Step 2 gives $q^{j/2}$ for the same absolute value; since $q>1$, $j=i$. Conversely, every reciprocal root of $P_{i,\ell}$ has a preimage $\alpha$ by step 5, and step 6 gives it some intrinsic weight $j$; the same equality forces $j=i$. The bijection thus restricts, with all repeated occurrences retained, to $\jmath(R_i)$ equal to the reciprocal-root multiset of $P_{i,\ell}$.

source.place: Step 5: both directions of the scalar root-multiset identification

proof.text: Map $Q_i=\prod_{\alpha\in R_i}(1-\alpha T)$ along $\jmath$. Finite-product compatibility in [lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-injective] gives $Q_i^{(\ell,\jmath)}=\prod_{\alpha\in R_i}(1-\jmath(\alpha)T)$. By step 8 its factors are exactly the reciprocal roots of $P_{i,\ell}$, with multiplicity. Clause (2) and the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization] therefore give $Q_i^{(\ell,\jmath)}=P_{i,\ell}$ in $K[T]$. Also $Q_i(0)=\prod_{\alpha\in R_i}1=1$, including when $R_i$ is empty. Since $Q_i$ has integer coefficients and every realization fixes $\mathbf Q$, this coefficientwise image agrees with the image along $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Q_\ell\to K$. Injectivity of $\mathbf Q_\ell[T]\to K[T]$ gives $Q_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ already in $\mathbf Q_\ell[T]$. This holds for every prime and every realization, so [def-weil-integral-frobenius-factor] applies. The construction of $R_i$ and $Q_i$ involved only the fixed $A,B$, $q$ and intrinsic weights, so it is independent of all these realization choices. Together with step 4 this proves every clause.

source.place: Step 5: polynomial equality, normalization, and realization independence

proof_origin.place: Steps 1-5 and embedded Intrinsic weights proof; expanded using existing DAG statements, with normalized fraction already assumed

proof.text:
*Step 1: the point counts are independent of $\ell$.* The
setting is the smooth, proper, geometrically connected $X_0/k_0$ of
pure dimension $d$ of [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses], in the
datums of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and the
integer point counts $N_n(X_0)=\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ do not
involve $\ell$, by the point-count convention of
[def-weil-point-counts-zeta]; hence the zeta series
$Z(X_0,T)$ lies in $1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]$, and by the closed-point
product of [prop-euler-product] it is the Taylor series of the
closed-point product. For each $\ell\neq p$, the point-count trace
formula of [cor-trf-point-counting] and the
[lem-zl-log-det-identity] log-determinant identity yield the
[thm-zl-lefschetz-weil-identity] trace-to-determinant identity

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_{i,\ell}(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}
\quad\text{in }\Ql[[T]],
$$

after the scalar extension to the $\Ql$-coefficients of
[def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family], with the root
convention of [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots]. Since the
right-hand side is rational over $\Ql$, its Taylor coefficients
satisfy a linear recurrence over $\Ql$, and its
[def-weil-hankel-matrix] has some finite rank $r$ over $\Ql$.
Every finite minor of order $r+1$ has integer entries and
vanishes in $\Ql$, hence already in $\mathbf Q$.
Thus its rank over $\mathbf Q$ is at most $r$, and by the
rationality criterion of
[prop-weil-rationality-criterion] the series lies in
$\mathbf Q(T)$; the normalized reduced integral presentation of
[def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction] is then the unique one
supplied by [prop-weil-zeta-normalized-presentation].

*Step 2: weight separation.* By [prop-weil-reciprocal-roots-eigenvalues]
the reciprocal roots of $P_{i,\ell}$ are the eigenvalues of
$F_{i,\ell}$, and [thm-weil-deligne-purity] gives
$|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$ for every such eigenvalue, for the fixed
isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ used there.
The hypotheses of [prop-weight-separation] therefore hold:
every reciprocal root of $P_{i,\ell}$ satisfies
$|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$, and the trace-to-determinant identity of
Step 1 holds. Concretely, the polynomials $P_{i,\ell}$,
$P_{j,\ell}$ are coprime for $i\neq j$, the parity products
$N_\ell,D_\ell$ of [def-weil-parity-products]
are coprime with constant coefficient $1$,
$Z(X_0,T)=N_\ell(T)/D_\ell(T)$, and the ordinary root multiset of
each $P_{i,\ell}$ is exactly the submultiset of roots of the
appropriate parity product with the weight-$i$ absolute-value
condition.

*Step 3: the parity products are the normalized presentation.*
Both $A^{(\ell)}/B^{(\ell)}$ and $N_\ell/D_\ell$ are reduced
fractions —$\gcd(A,B)=1$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$ by
[def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction], $\gcd(N_\ell,D_\ell)=1$
by Step 2 —with constant coefficients $1$, and both equal the
Taylor series $Z(X_0,T)$ in $\Ql[[T]]$. Cross multiplication
and coprimality over $\Ql[T]$ show that the numerators and
denominators differ by the same scalar. Their constant terms
are $1$, so that scalar is $1$. Consequently
$A^{(\ell)}=N_\ell$ and $B^{(\ell)}=D_\ell$ coefficientwise in
$\Ql$, after extension along the [def-weil-algebraic-closure-q]
identification $\jmath_\ell$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]'s
datum. This is the parity-product clause.

*Step 4: the weight strata and the stratum polynomials.* By
*Intrinsic weights of the reciprocal roots* below, every root of $A^\#$ or $B^\#$ has a
unique weight in $\{0,\ldots,2d\}$, and the resulting root multisets
$R_i$ are Galois-stable. Hence
[prop-galois-weight-strata-integrality] and
[prop-galois-weight-strata-identification] apply and return that the
normalized stratum polynomials

$$
Q_i(T)=\prod_{\alpha\in R_i}(1-\alpha T)
$$

lie in $\mathbf Z[T]$ and that the reciprocal-root multiset of $Q_i$
is the weight-$i$ submultiset of the roots of $A^\#$
($i$ odd) or of $B^\#$ ($i$ even). This is the integrality clause
for the stratum polynomials.

*Step 5: the scalar identities.* For fixed
$\ell\neq p$ and $\jmath_\ell$, the scalar extension
$Q_i^{(\ell,\jmath_\ell)}$ is the product over the identified
weight-$i$ submultiset of roots of $A^{(\ell)\#}=N_\ell^\#$
($i$ odd) or of $B^{(\ell)\#}=D_\ell^\#$ ($i$ even), which by
the multiset identification of Step 2 is exactly the reciprocal-root
multiset of $P_{i,\ell}$; both polynomials have constant
coefficient $1$, so

$$
Q_i^{(\ell,\jmath_\ell)}(T)=P_{i,\ell}(T),
$$

the identity of the interface statement. The independence of the
identity from the chosen realization and realization isomorphism is
the uniqueness in Step 4, and $Q_i(0)=1$ is the normalization
$Q_i(0)=\prod_{\alpha\in R_i}1=1$. With Step 3 this establishes
the assertion, and $Q_i$ is the integral Frobenius factor of
[def-weil-integral-frobenius-factor]
in degree $i$: its scalar extension along $\jmath_\ell$ is
$P_{i,\ell}$ for every $\ell\neq p$.

**Intrinsic weights of the reciprocal roots.** In the situation of [thm-weil-realization-independence], every root of
$A^\#$ or $B^\#$ has a unique weight in $\{0,\ldots,2d\}$, and the
resulting multisets $R_i$ of
ordinary roots that are
$q$-Weil numbers of weight $i$ are stable
under $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q)$.

*Proof.*
In the situation of [thm-weil-realization-independence] the fraction
$A^{(\ell)}/B^{(\ell)}$ and the parity products $N_\ell/D_\ell$ of
[prop-weight-separation] both equal the series $Z(X_0,T)$ in
$\Ql[[T]]$; here $\gcd(A,B)=1$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$ by
[def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction], while $\gcd(N_\ell,D_\ell)=1$
and $N_\ell(0)=D_\ell(0)=1$ by [prop-weight-separation]. Cross
multiplication over $\Ql[T]$ and coprimality therefore give
$A^{(\ell)}=N_\ell$ and $B^{(\ell)}=D_\ell$. Hence every root of
$A^\#$ or $B^\#$ maps under $\jmath_\ell$ to a root of $N_\ell^\#$
or $D_\ell^\#$ in the [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots]
convention, that is, to a reciprocal root of exactly one of the factors
$P_{i,\ell}$ (distinct $P_{i,\ell}$ being coprime by
[prop-weight-separation]); the weight of that factor is a weight of
the root, because every root of $P_{i,\ell}$ has absolute value
$q^{i/2}$ by [prop-weight-purity-roots] and an arbitrary complex
embedding of the number field generated by the root extends to an
isomorphism of algebraic closures by [lem-embedding-extension]. For
the same reason the weight is independent of the chosen $\ell$ and
realization, the $q$-Weil condition of [def-weil-numbers] being
stable under $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q)$ and
under every embedding of its number field into $\mathbf C$; the
conditions of distinct weights are mutually exclusive because
$q^{i/2}\neq q^{j/2}$ for $i\neq j$. Each root of $A^\#$ or $B^\#$
therefore has a unique weight in $\{0,\ldots,2d\}$, and the multisets
$R_i$ of [thm-weil-realization-independence] are stable under
$\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q)$.
